children: Uber Technologies Inc. (UBER, Financials) the ride-hailing and delivery company, has got a big vote of confidence from one of the executives operating the business.
President and Chief Operating Officer Andrew Macdonald bought 70,000 shares for about $5.3 million. He paid between $75.23 and $76.85 a share

That's not your average type of purchase. And the timing is uncanny. Uber shares recently traded around $73 after dropping 3.5% Tuesday. The corporation is also in a period of transition, with job layoffs and a rising push into driverless mobility.
That left investors with a familiar question: Can Uber keep growing as the ride-hailing market shifts underneath it? Macdonald looks happy to put his own money behind that gamble.
Insider buying isn't a sure fire way to push up a stock price. Executives are wrong just like everybody else.
Still, it's impossible to dismiss a $5.3 million open-market purchase by Uber's president and COO, especially while the stock is under pressure.
The next thing for investors to watch is if Uber's operating performance begins to back up that optimism as the business balances cost cutting, growth and its autonomous car strategy.

title: Uber's No. 2 Executive Just Put $5.3 Million Into the Stock
